podcast.body: Released on August 16, 1989, the cover of *Mother's Milk* features a black and white photograph of a giant, topless woman, Don Lane, cradling all four band members in her arms, with a rose covering her left nipple. The original idea came from Anthony Kiedis, inspired by a 1970s Sly and the Family Stone poster he had as a child. Guitarist John Frusciante proved difficult during the photoshoot, rejecting all but one photo of himself laughing. Although Ioni Skye, Anthony Kiedis's girlfriend at the time, was also photographed, Don Lane's image was ultimately chosen. "A black and white photo of a giant, topless woman, cradling all four members of the band in her arms with her left nipple covered by a rose."

podcast.body: Released on August 16, 1989, this album marked a significant breakthrough for the band. It followed a challenging period that included the death of guitarist Hillel Slovak from a heroin overdose and issues with successive drummers. Their unique punk-funk sound, initially ahead of its time, finally found its audience by the summer of 1989. "On August 16, 1989, the Red Hot Chili Peppers finally caught a break with their fourth album called Mother's Milk."

podcast.body: This album marked the debut of John Frusciante as guitarist and Chad Smith as drummer, forming what would become the classic Red Hot Chili Peppers lineup. Frusciante contributed nine songs to the album, though his style was still evolving and influenced by producer Michael Beinhorn to be heavier than his natural inclination. The album served as an early showcase for Frusciante's emerging melodic style. "John was drafted in to complete the guitar parts for the new album Mother's Milk."
